content: Classic DB-backed queue bug: SELECT-then-UPDATE to claim a job is a race condition -- two workers can grab the same row, causing duplicate processing (e.g., duplicate notifications). Fix: atomic claim via UPDATE...OUTPUT with row-level locking hints (SQL Server: ROWLOCK, READPAST, UPDLOCK in a single statement; Postgres: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). All job handlers must still be idempotent because at-least-once delivery is the norm even with atomic claims (a worker can crash after committing side effects but before marking the job done). Stuck jobs: a worker that crashes mid-job leaves rows stuck in 'running' forever unless a reaper/heartbeat process resets stale locks after a timeout.
